description: Cups, spoons and milliliters — plus grams via ingredient density.

faqs.a: Cups, tablespoons, teaspoons, fluid ounces, milliliters and liters. Volume is converted first, then multiplied by the ingredient's density to get grams.
faqs.q: Which units and ingredients are supported?

faqs.a: Densities are typical averages (e.g. all-purpose flour ≈ 0.53 g/ml). Brands and packing vary, so treat the gram weight as an estimate, not a lab measurement.
faqs.q: How accurate are the gram weights?

faqs.a: 1 US cup = 236.588 ml. Note that some countries use a 250 ml metric cup.
faqs.q: How many milliliters are in a cup?

howto: Enter the amount in the first field.
Pick the volume unit you are converting from.
Choose the ingredient to apply its density.
Read the volume in every unit plus the estimated weight in grams.
